raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through.

I've been working this land for fifty years — my father and grandfather worked it before me. It's just me and my wife at home now; our children moved to the city years ago and send money back sometimes, but the farming is on our shoulders. Twenty-five mu isn't small but it isn't big either. For two old people, it's about right if we use the machinery contractors for the heavy work. I can't bend over all day like I used to.

Like everyone around here, I do wheat then maize on the same ground. The wheat goes in after the maize comes off in October, and the maize goes in right after the wheat comes off in June — sometimes the same day, because if you wait a week you lose yield. That turnaround is the hardest part of the year.

For wheat, I always use the compound fertilizer (复合肥) as a base before I plow — about one bag (50 kg) per mu, that's 15-15-15 or sometimes 18-18-18 when the shop has it. Then when the wheat starts jointing in spring, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu, more if the color looks pale. The extension man from the county came a few years back and said we use too much nitrogen, but I don't trust going too low — I saw what happened to my neighbor Old Wang when he cut back, his yield dropped badly that year. Better to spend a little more on fertilizer than lose 50 kg of wheat per mu.

Water: the well is ours to share with three families on this lane, and pumping costs money — maybe 25-30 yuan per mu each time. For wheat I irrigate at winter (保墒水), green-up (返青水), jointing (拔节水), and grain-filling (灌浆水) — that's four times normally. If it rains well in spring I might skip one. For maize, usually the rains come in July-August and I don't irrigate at all, but if there's a dry spell at tasseling, I'll put on one or two waterings because that stage you cannot miss.

Seeds — I buy improved wheat variety at the co-op, Jimai or Shiluan series, whatever they're pushing that year. For maize I use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid, about 2 kg seed per mu. I don't save seed anymore, the hybrids don't come back true.

Pesticide: I spray herbicide both crops, that's standard now. For maize I watch for armyworm and corn borer — if I see them I spray, if not I don't bother. At my age I'm not climbing around the field every day checking.

I expect maybe 450 kg wheat and 500 kg maize per mu this year if the weather behaves. That's what I usually get. I'm not chasing big yields — I want steady.
